Excellent course that changed how I think about technology and society. Prof. Vashistha is insightful, approachable, and makes every class discussion meaningful. Readings are strong and relevant. Workload is manageable. Best for students interested in AI, HCI, ethics, or global impact.

One of the most thought-provoking classes I took at Cornell. Prof. Vashistha is engaging and genuinely cares about students. Great discussions on AI, tech, and global development. Workload is fair but there are readings each week. Not coding-heavy. Highly recommend if you want to think deeply.

This was one of the best courses I have attended. The course opened up completely new perspectives on me and the learning will help me regardless of what I do next.

analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: By all means the best professor I have ever had. Not only is he absolutely dapper, he is exciting, reflective, sharp as a knife and very very interested in his students. Every lecture made me question my own assumptions about democracy, civility, punishment and social justice and always left me inspired, motivated and provoked. Take his class!!

the course i took was actually GOVT 2785, Civil Disobedience. he's very funny and gives good lectures that are pretty engaging, though i would say that the format can be a little repetitive as he mainly just summarizes the readings, though he does give good background information/context that can be very useful. we had two prelims and one final.

Livingston is an wonderful teacher and an incredible human being. He taught GOVT 3675 at 8:40 AM this past semester, and I stumbled in bleary-eyed but excited for his lectures. Taking GOVT 3675, I felt like I learned an incredible amount and that my interest in political theory skyrocketed. All because of the wonderful teacher that is Livingston.

I've never had a professor that moderated discussions better than Livingston. His probing questions made the readings fascinating, and I was always excited to come to class and discuss democracy. He was very funny and nice, and a fair grader - hands down one of my favorite professors. I only wish I could've taken more classes with him.

Professor Livingston is a really remarkable professor who enables students to develop their own perspective and ideas through his wonderful lectures. I had a truly transformative experience in GOVT 3675, much of which was due to Livingstons fascinating lectures.

analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: This class was interesting. It is definitely reading and test-heavy, but if you give a good amount of effort and are also interested in the content, then you'll be able to do well. I took this class for a major req but ended up liking it a lot. You're only graded on a few things, so definitely important to keep up well and take notes every lecture.

Professor Willford was enthusiastic which helped make lectures more engaging. Lectures aren't recorded and have minimalist slides, so although lectures aren't required, I recommend going. The class has a lot of reading but he summarizes it well in lecture, so skimming was fine. We ended behind syllabus so stuff was cut out and exams weren't bad.

Def lecture heavy. Lots of readings, helps a lot if you keep up with them, but he will eventually review them in class. Goes off-track with talking, ends up with no time for questions. Genuinely very kind and helpful + TA is awesome. Sections help with interpreting what he says in class. Not sure how attendance was marked, but accounts for 20%.

Lectures were pretty boring, but the readings were great. If I fell asleep in any class, it was this one. I would give it a 3 but the sections on religion and acts of terror (e.g. dramatical violence) made the course overall informative and enjoyable. I would watch out if you get this professor with a more boring subject, however.

Good person, has a tendency to get distracted during lecture, but that didn't hurt my ability to do assignments. A ton of readings, but you can really just cherrypick certain chapters/concepts if you can't fully commit to reading everything. Always happy to engage and answer questions.

analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

review_highlights.comment: anke is a fantastic cs2800 professor, definitely take it with her. lectures were extremely well prepared and interesting. the hw and prelims are definitely challenging, but they help you understand material at a deeper level and are still fairly manageable.

Very nice and knowledgeable professor. Discrete math is not easy but very interesting imo, and her lectures made it understandable (especially after reading the textbook). Stay ahead with textbook readings!! Homework was hard, I recommend submitting it in LaTeX format since TAs prefer it. Tests and weekly quizzes are also hard, but you learn a lot.

The class was definitely difficult, but Professor Anke really tried her best to break down the concepts and make them easy to understand. Great lectures and lecture notes. The curve is definitely really generous considering I got F's on both my prelims when the median was roughly a 70, and I got median on the final. Overall glad this class is over!

Anke's lectures are really amazing and she explains difficult concepts very well. Her poll questions help ease you into the concepts. Hws and discussion problems can be hard especially if this is your first time with proofs, but are very helpful. Sometimes the grading is a bit strict, but couldn't recommend taking this class with her more.

A great prof for a great class! Lectures are engaging and the poll questions are great to test your understanding. Homeworks, quizzes, and exams are well-written, and the grading is quite fair. The course textbook is really great, and the practice exercises are great for exam prep. Her office hours are also very accessible.

She is actually the worst teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are uninformative, so you have to figure everything out yourself. She makes the homeworks impossible and super time consuming. Does not "believe" in giving 100s. Soft spoken, but speaks audaciously to children, students, and all. Very strict classroom rules. No leeway for attendance. Thought the class content was okay and easy, but disliked it purely because of her.

I really liked the course content, but the professor ruined it. She is so picky with wording and leaves the craziest revision comments on essays. She is extremely up-tight and allows no room for creativity. She will take off points if you come in a second late and will ridicule you in front of the entire class. Her expectations are at times unclear and the assignments themselves are largely unrelated to the class.

As a management class, this has been one of the worst-managed and least-organized classes I have ever taken at Cornell. It's great that she's so passionate about the subject matter, but vague lectures, poorly-defined grading criteria and a lack of awareness of how much work she assigns are massive detriments to her teaching style. Bad website, too.

Professor Burton is very enthusiastic about students but she speaks VERY fast and to be honest, she's not a very good teacher. She's hardly clear and very difficult to follow. This professor's employment makes the school look like a joke. The most disorganized and unfair professor I've ever encountered. The presentation we worked on for 3 months had no weight. Fire her

While Professor Burton is lovely, ILRID 1700 was among the least organized of my Cornell career. There is a ton of weight on group work, making it almost impossible to succeed if you get a bad group (speaking from experience) and lectures are generally all over the place. review_highlights.comment: Clermont is a brilliant scholar but unable to make the material understandable for his students.  Lectures go off on irrelevant tangents, leaving less time for important material.  The exam was absolutely ridiculous and does not measure how well the students learned the semester's material.  Sorry Cornell 1Ls, you're stuck with him one semester.

Go on the journey Clermont wants you to go on and you will be more than okay. Write down everything he says in class and build your outline from that. The MCQ exam had some curveballs, but also a lot of questions that were completely fair and doable if you paid attention. Just don't give up and into the fear mongering.

I aced Clermont's class but the one thing I'll note is that his class is very lecture focused. Random iClicker questions, previous practice problems, and off-the-cuff lecture tangents morph into exam questions so you sort of need to write down everything he says. Being old school he's also purposefully opaque. And the textbook? LMAO.

Clermont is a genius who is unable to translate this genius into good pedagogy. His exams are more like riddles of the Sphinx than measures of his students' understanding of the material. Funny guy though.
He knows literally everything about civil procedure and is a genius. He is not for everyone. But if he's your style, you will see the law in a new way.

analysis.name: Bruce Ganem
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ganem is easily one of the best professors at this university. His lectures are direct and inspiring, and he truly gives you all the tools you need to do well in the class, if you work hard. Weekly practice is your best friend in this course. Also, pay attention in lecture, and you will be able to predict what will be big on the exams.

A lot of reviews have said that some material he tested on were not included in lecture. I disagree. Sure, some of the questions were difficult, but I would qualify them more as "thinking cap" questions, where we've seen a similar mechanism in lecture but on the test it was slightly different. TLDR, pay attention in lecture and you should be fine.

His lectures are good and cover everything you need for the test. His tests were generally fair. Curve is generous and better than gen chem. If you go for 1 on 1 office hours with Dr. Ganem, he's very condescending which doesn't help so it's best to learn what you can in lecture and use the TAs for outside help. Great teacher, meh person.

I loved Dr. Ganem even though I didn't get the best grade in honors orgo. I learned so much and he is genuinely such a cool guy. Please go to office hours to learn more about him if you have the chance because he has super cool stories and a very effective one-on-one / small group teaching style as well that you don't get from lectures.

I personally didn't find Ganem's lectures to be very helpful. Most of my learning came from taking the support class (highly recommended!), going to the learning center, and using outside resources like the organic chemistry as a second language textbook. The exams are difficult, but the curve is very generous

review_highlights.comment: Yes the tests are really hard, but this class is very fair overall. Best formula to get an A: GO to lecture, write down about half of what he says, learn the bold terms in the book, and study hard for tests. Cutting is a masterful lecturer, very intelligent and knowledgeable. Boring every once in a while but usually fascinating, original material.
Knowledgable professor but he cannot communicate information clearly to students. Powerpoint slides are not very helpful. Prelims draw from pure memorization of random definitions.

His lecture slides by themselves are not too helpful. The real stuff happens in the professor's delivery in class. So attending lecture is key. If you make it, the lectures are fascinating and well-delivered; if you don't, well, good luck trying to infer the content from pictures and random terms. (When I tried that, it didn't go well.)

An incredibly thorough, clear, and well-organized teacher. Exams were detailed, but very fair. He also let the entire class know outright that lecture material and text readings would be distinct from one another, but that both would be covered on prelims. Hands-down one of the most competent people I've learned something from at Cornell.

I didn't read the textbooks, just did my best to memorize the glossary terms from the assigned readings. I took extremely detailed notes of everything he SAYS. Memorize everything you can. His delivery of the lecture was most important. I learned a lot in this class and appreciate Prof Cutting's dedication and passion for these topics :D

analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Perhaps one of the best professors at Cornell University. He not only demonstrates mastery over his content, but also delivers his lectures in a passionate and intelligent way. I would recommend everyone in AEM to take de Gorter's WTO class at some point in time.

Each week, he will assign readings; and in this seminar-style class, students will discuss the topic of the readings after he lectures for a little. There are a few exams and written assignments, and the "final exam" is a research paper on a trade dispute. It's not a terribly difficult class, but it requires some time commitment for the reading.
Phenomenal professor, incredibly organized. Felt like he was losing his mind toward the end of the class. Showing bad bunny clips right now.

The material was complex but De Gorter grades generously. We were graded on attendance, two pop quizzes (he warned us the class prior for both), two five page papers, a midterm, and a final. The final was an online take home exam.

I've taken both of his classes here. He literally exudes intelligence about the subject, and cares SO much about his students. He's really flexible with the grading portion, and really just focuses on our learning and applying the material! He's hilarious, and while a bit long-winded, will tailor your learning to your interests!
